description: Request header transform rules — publish edge-measured client facts to the origin. Deployed to the http_request_late_transform phase, NOT the response phase used by transform-rules.json: a request-header rewrite placed in the response phase is accepted by the API and never reaches the origin, so the signal would appear configured and stay silently absent.

rules.description: Publish the connecting client's autonomous-system number to the origin as X-Postwave-Client-ASN. subscriber_event_observations.network_asn was NULL on every row ever written because nothing supplied it, and the machine-source registry matches on that column — this rule is what makes the signal measurable at all. MUST be 'set', never 'add': the value has to OVERWRITE any client-supplied copy, and the origin refuses the header outright when it arrives more than once. This rule is necessary but NOT sufficient: the origin honours the header only when the TCP peer is inside POSTWAVE_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS and POSTWAVE_TRUST_FORWARDED_IP_HEADERS is enabled, so a header arriving from anywhere else is ignored rather than believed. Without that second half an attacker could choose their own ASN and therefore their own human/machine classification.
